name: Kaiming Liu
title: Physics PhD student
description: Kaiming Liu is a Physics PhD student at UIUC studying scientific machine learning, probabilistic inverse problems, and computational condensed matter physics.
bio: My research uses scientific machine learning for inverse problems, focusing on probabilistic inference and simulation-to-experiment robustness. I previously worked in experimental condensed matter physics.
background: Before moving to computation, I worked in Vidya Madhavan’s group at UIUC, growing thin films with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and studying electronic structure with STM/STS in ultrahigh vacuum (UHV). I also developed experimental automation and Python/MATLAB analysis of quasiparticle-interference data.
interests: Scientific machine learning; inverse problems; probabilistic inference; simulation-to-experiment transfer; computational condensed matter physics.

education.degree: Special Class for the Gifted Young

experience.role: Graduate researcher, Bryan K. Clark group

projects.title: Crystal-field inverse modeling
bullets: Represent non-unique crystal-field solutions from susceptibility with residual-MLP conditional Gaussian mixture models.
Validate candidates by reconstructing susceptibility; test training noise on synthetic curves and experimental measurements.

projects.title: Magnetic-scattering inverse modeling
bullets: Infer exchange parameters from powder-averaged neutron-scattering maps using MLP and ResNet conditional Gaussian mixtures.
Use exact Sunny forward checks and classical fits as references; test sensitivity to noise, intensity scale, and background offsets.

projects.title: Neural-network backflow / variational Monte Carlo
bullets: Implement JAX neural-network backflow wavefunctions and variational Monte Carlo for lattice Hubbard models.
Profile parallel GPU sampling, local-energy evaluation, and gradient synchronization; check chunked evaluation against the original computation.
Grew thin-film heterostructures with MBE and characterized electronic structure using STM/STS in ultrahigh vacuum.
Automated growth temperature control and built Python/MATLAB analysis of STM/STS quasiparticle-interference data.
Simulated Rydberg-atom dynamics and photon-mediated interactions in Python/MATLAB to study quantum nonlinear optics.
Built a discrete-time lattice model of two-qubit phase-flip dynamics and many-body regimes.

experience.role: Research assistant, Michael F. Crommie group
bullets: Assisted synthesis and STM characterization of graphene nanoribbons with five-membered rings to study their electronic states.

teaching.text: Led discussion and laboratory sections, held office hours, and provided feedback on assignments in electromagnetism and modern physics.

honors.name: Mathematical Contest in Modeling, Meritorious Winner

skills.items: Python (PyTorch, JAX, NumPy, SciPy), MATLAB; conditional mixture models; Git, Linux.
MCMC, variational Monte Carlo, numerical optimization; GPU/cluster computation and runtime profiling.
MBE, STM/STS, ultrahigh vacuum, feedback control, experimental automation and data analysis.

researchProfile: Scientific machine learning for magnetic inverse problems: probabilistic models, physical forward validation, and simulation-to-experiment robustness. Background in experimental condensed matter and computational many-body physics.
